title: Lower-and-upper-bound sandwich for the Fuchs-van de Graaf inequalities
intent: Assemble the Fuchs-van de Graaf inequalities, the two-sided comparison 1 − F ≤ D ≤ √(1 − F²) between trace distance D and quantum fidelity F, as a conjunction of a lower bound and an upper bound, each proved by its own dedicated lemma, and close the whole by `exact ⟨fuchsVanDeGraaf_lower rho sigma, fuchsVanDeGraaf_upper rho sigma⟩`.

parent.name: fuchsVanDeGraafInequalities
parent.statement:
theorem fuchsVanDeGraafInequalities (rho sigma : State d) :
    1 - QITBench.OneShot.quantumFidelity rho.matrix sigma.matrix ≤
        traceDistance rho sigma ∧
      traceDistance rho sigma ≤
        Real.sqrt
          (1 - (QITBench.OneShot.quantumFidelity rho.matrix sigma.matrix) ^ 2)

applicability.goal_shape: A conjunction P ≤ x ∧ x ≤ Q (a two-sided bound / sandwich) where x is a distance- or norm-like quantity and P, Q are two different functions of a shared parameter (here the quantum fidelity F): P = 1 − F and Q = √(1 − F²).
applicability.use_when: each side has an independent, self-contained proof (here two long matrix-norm developments) and the two bounds are genuinely different expressions, so neither an iff-split nor an order antisymmetry (both directions are a ≤ b and b ≤ a) applies; the conjunction is then closed by one `exact ⟨lower, upper⟩`.
applicability.avoid_when: the two sides share a substantial argument that is not first lifted into a private lemma (here the SVD / trace-norm / frobenius infrastructure is factored out first, so each side only assembles it); or when only one side is nontrivial and the other follows by a one-liner such as `linarith`; or when the statement is a single inequality rather than a pair.
